claims.quote: Then, in most places, one or other, perhaps two will come in sight.
claims.description: Launch an artificial moon made of brick into orbit so ships can be seen against it and determine their longitude.

claims.quote: Upward and northward it would rise, therefore, till it had passed the axis of the world.
claims.description: Launch the brick satellite by rolling it onto two counter-rotating giant flywheels that store power and fling it upward into orbit.

claims.quote: Now let it fall," said Q., inspired with the vision. "Let it fall, and the sooner the better! The curve it is now on will forever clear the world;
claims.description: An object thrown fast enough from Earth will fall into a stable orbit that clears the planet forever, circling above the poles and fixed meridians.

claims.quote: But at four thousand miles' distance the moon could be seen by a belt of observers six or eight thousand miles in diameter.
claims.description: Place two or four such artificial moons in orbit to give near-global visibility for navigation.

claims.quote: if on the old Thornbush moon old Herschel with his reflector could see a town-house two hundred feet long, on the Brick Moon young Herschel will be able to see a dab of mortar a foot and a half long
claims.description: Telescopes could resolve tiny details on the artificial moon from Earth.

claims.quote: He had unlimited freezing power. So have we now, as we had not then. With this power he made an ice lens, ten feet in diameter,
claims.description: A giant ten-foot ice lens, rubbed to precise shape, serves as a telescope objective surpassing glass lenses.

claims.quote: Let me hope that before next winter passes some countryman or countrywoman of mine will have equalled his success, and with an ice lens will surpass all the successes of the glasses of our time.
claims.description: Predicts that ice-lens telescopes could soon exceed the performance of the best glass telescopes.
